feed and basis: Two study-specific waste categories EVAc and MP; smallest class F4
direct silver evidence: Yes: Ag partition into the finest fraction reported
reported metrics: Up to 70% and 80% of total feed Ag in F4 for EVAc and MP, respectively; EV-011: 94.12% of Ag reported in the <0.25 mm fine fraction
what was actually measured: Study-specific Ag distribution across sieved fractions; a separate 2024 polycrystalline-module study reported Ag concentrated in fine fractions
what remains unreported: Accessible abstract does not supply absolute feed mass, product mass, product grade or full uncertainty
environmental/practical evidence: Avoided thermal burning in the proposed method; no numerical energy or dust-control data
comparability limits: Different module categories and sieve bins; cannot assume same distribution for AGASTYA; 2024 result uses a separate polycrystalline feed and cannot be averaged with the 2022 categories
AGASTYA assessment: Strong simple comparator for Stage 2; test actual size-dependent Ag partition before adding Stage 3

route description: Mechanical liberation followed by electrostatic separation
feed and basis: Mechanically processed polycrystalline PV scraps in de Souza and Veit; a separate c-Si silicon-target study by Li et al.
direct silver evidence: Direct co-concentration of Ag, Al and Si reported in EV-003; no accessible mass-based Ag recovery or grade
reported metrics: EV-003: 38 kV and 75 rpm; 49.22% of input material in the smallest below-0.5-mm size class. EV-004: 91.0% Si proportion and 48.9% Si recovery, not Ag.
what was actually measured: XRF elemental proportions; another study measured Si recovery
what remains unreported: Silver recovery, silver product grade, full product masses, particle charge distribution and uncertainty in accessible abstract
environmental/practical evidence: No lifecycle energy or emissions data extracted; electrostatic voltage and feed-size requirements are study-specific
comparability limits: Do not infer Ag recovery from Si recovery; co-concentration does not equal Ag selectivity; equipment and feed differ
AGASTYA assessment: Mechanism is plausible and has direct but incomplete Ag evidence. Retain only as a testable candidate, not a validated selective stage.

route description: Mechanical liberation followed by silver-focused froth flotation
feed and basis: 3.5 kg prepared, delaminated and crushed solar-cell feed; feed grade is cell-feed grade, not whole-module grade
direct silver evidence: Yes: ICP-MS assays of feed, concentrate and tailings; fire assay cross-check
reported metrics: Tap-water rougher 97.55 +/- 0.03% Ag recovery and 32.2 +/- 2.3 upgrade; rougher-cleaner 46.7 +/- 1.5 wt% Ag at 86.5 +/- 2.8% recovery
what was actually measured: Silver assays and concentration/recovery in a bench flotation campaign
what remains unreported: AGASTYA feed response, lifecycle economics, full-scale water/energy burden and continuous operation
environmental/practical evidence: 150 g/t reagent dosage reported; bench slurry water; no complete lifecycle inventory
comparability limits: Strongest direct Ag evidence but different cell feed, size reduction, reagents and trained laboratory context
AGASTYA assessment: Best direct evidence comparator for silver-specific beneficiation; not suitable to copy as a school process or predict Agastya yield.

route description: Mechanical liberation followed by chemical extraction/refining
feed and basis: EV-001 waste c-Si modules; EV-006 prepared and milled silicon-cell feed
direct silver evidence: Yes: author-reported silver concentration/extraction and product assay
reported metrics: EV-001 reports 94% silver yield without pyrolysis and 92% with pyrolysis; EV-006 reports about 98% overall Ag recovery and >99.9% product purity
what was actually measured: Study-specific extraction, residue assays and/or product composition
what remains unreported: Comparable feed basis, reproducible independent mass balances for this project, AGASTYA process safety, waste-treatment and cost data
environmental/practical evidence: Acids, precipitation/reduction reagents, heating and effluent management; no complete lifecycle or cost result
comparability limits: Cell/module feed, initial grade, analytical method and process endpoints differ; cannot compare percentages as a single ranking
AGASTYA assessment: Strong silver extraction evidence but outside the proposed dry four-stage train and requires a properly supervised facility.

route description: Thermal delamination pretreatment followed by mechanical separation
feed and basis: Single decommissioned 370 Wp mono module coupons for EV-008; modeled full-size module for EV-010
reported metrics: EV-008: n=6 at each temperature, residue morphology differed; EV-010: comparative delamination-site simulation
what was actually measured: Glass peel and material morphology in coupons; numerical cohesive-zone damage in another work
what remains unreported: Ag partition, energy per panel, Ag feed preservation and AGASTYA-specific adhesion behavior
environmental/practical evidence: Thermal time and possible energy; no lifecycle figures in retrieved studies
comparability limits: Not a silver concentration route; coupon and simulation interfaces are study-specific
AGASTYA assessment: Optional pretreatment to be compared with nonthermal liberation; do not label as Stage 3 under current architecture.
